entities.summary: Nicanor of Stageira was a Macedonian diplomat and courier who played a crucial role in the administration of Alexander the Great's vast empire. In 324 BCE, Nicanor was despatched by Alexander to proclaim the decree for the recall of exiles throughout the Greek cities, a move that would have significant implications for the Hellenistic world. This event marked a turning point in the history of the Greek city-states, as it would lead to the re-establishment of their autonomy and the reinvigoration of their cultural and political institutions. Nicanor's mission also underscored the centralizing ambitions of Alexander, who sought to reorganize the ancient world according to his own vision of a unified, Hellenized empire. The legacy of Nicanor's mission can be seen in the enduring influence of Greek culture on the Mediterranean world, as well as the complex web of alliances and rivalries that would shape the Hellenistic period.
